hints.title: Word Segmentation Subproblem Ordering
hints.text: A concatenated word must be composed entirely of shorter valid dictionary words. Sorting words by length enables building valid prefixes progressively.

hints.title: Prefix Composition Invariant
hints.text: Word w can be formed if there exists some split index k such that prefix w[:k] can be formed and suffix w[k:] is an existing dictionary word.

hints.title: Length Sorted Dynamic Search Procedure
hints.text: Sort all words ascending by length. For each word, check if it can be segmented into words currently present in the seen dictionary using standard word break validation. If valid, record it in the results list; otherwise add the word into the seen dictionary set.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input length or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N * L^2) time and O(N * L) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs or subsegment combinations without length ordering leads to cyclic dependencies and high exponential overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting by length and testing segmentation takes O(N * L^2) time using O(N * L) set storage for previously inspected words.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that sorting by length guarantees that potential sub-words are always processed before the compound word.
